input.cause: procedure.submit has a schema (checked before any guard) that requires every data/abort entry to carry a numeric threshold. The refusals name only abort entries 1 and 2 (entry 0 passes). Step 8 also names data/occupancy. In the guard's own refusals in other tasks, the required abort conditions include "co2" and "refused", and "refused" is not a numeric limit. I infer that the model left the threshold off, or sent it as a non-number, on abort entries that have no natural number. The sent arguments are "(not kept)", so this is not shown directly. The refusal text is true but tells the model only the type, not what to put for a condition without a limit. The same form came back 7 times in 2 tasks (haiku), across two prompt fingerprints, 433bbb9878a7 and 8cc0cfd05ef9. So it is not a regression from a prompt change. It is a gap between the schema and the texts the model reads, not a guard rule.
